summary.scope:
Measure raw-stress reward repeatability and paired grasp-force discrimination.

Each of eight frozen conditions is duplicated with only the commanded strong
grip force limit changed. The original approach/lift/slide/weak/release schedule,
arm targets, radii, friction and resets are retained. Intrusive observations
make this a behavioral experiment, never a throughput benchmark.
summary.limitations: Raw stress and exposure are uncalibrated reward proxies for two explicitly controlled grip choices. This is numerical repeatability and useful discrimination conditional on the chosen480-tet mesh, actual rigid contact and model/radius assumptions. It does not certify a fracture threshold, physical stress accuracy or complete RL training. Different models can change stress rankings without changing rigid motion. All values and any rejected input remain; intrusive observer timing is excluded from throughput.
